original_question: For a fixed prime p and any real number theta, must one always have lim inf_{q -> +infty} q |q|_p ||q theta|| = 0? Equivalently, for irrational theta, is it true or false that inf_{n,q in Z_+} q ||p^n q theta|| = 0?
target_in_paper: Section 1, subsection "p-adic version of Littlewood conjecture": the unnumbered de Mathan-Teulié p-adic (mixed) Littlewood conjecture, together with its explicit reformulation for irrational θ.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target very closely: it fixes a prime p, quantifies over all real θ, states the liminf form q|q|_p||qθ||, and includes the exact equivalent reformulation that the paper itself gives for irrational θ in terms of inf_{n,q in Z_+} q||p^n qθ||.
missing_details: The paper defines ||x|| as the distance from x to the nearest integer.
The paper explicitly defines the p-adic norm on integers: if n = p^ν n_1 with (n_1,p)=1, then |n|_p = p^{-ν}.
It should be made explicit that q (and n in the reformulation) range over positive integers Z_+.
The equivalent reformulation is stated only for irrational θ, not for all real θ.
To be fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, the question should name the problem as the p-adic or mixed Littlewood conjecture.
It helps to specify that q -> +infty means along positive integers.
refined_question: Fix a prime number p. Let ||x|| denote the distance from x to the nearest integer, and for a positive integer q write q = p^{ν_p(q)}q_1 with gcd(q_1,p)=1, so that |q|_p = p^{-ν_p(q)}. Is it true that for every real number θ one has lim inf_{q -> +infty, q in Z_+} q |q|_p ||qθ|| = 0? This is the de Mathan-Teulié p-adic (mixed) Littlewood conjecture.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as stated in the paper, for irrational θ is it true that inf_{n,q in Z_+} q ||p^n qθ|| = 0?
justification: The draft is aiming at the core mixed/p-adic Littlewood conjecture as stated in Section 1 of the paper, not at the later metric theorem (Theorem 4) or the two-prime consequence discussed immediately afterward. In the subsection "p-adic version of Littlewood conjecture," Moshchevitin first defines the p-adic norm |.|_p for a fixed prime p and then states the conjecture in the liminf form for every real θ. He immediately adds the reformulation for irrational θ in terms of inf_{n,q in Z_+} q||p^n qθ||. So the sharp paper-faithful standalone question is exactly this conjecture, with the notation made explicit.
